int.note: Default TEST_DATABASE_URL (localhost:5433) fails auth in this environment because a native Windows postgres.exe service is also bound to port 5433 alongside the Docker Postgres (confirmed via netstat: two different PIDs LISTENING on 5433, one docker-backend, one postgres.exe). Ran instead against the same Docker container's second published port (TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgresql://devscribed:devscribed@localhost:5434/devscribed_test), which is documented in test/database-url.ts as the supported override. No container, volume or service was touched.

e2e.note: First run (default/auto worker count) additionally showed 5 regressions.spec.ts failures and 3 flaky cases, all 30s page.goto/element timeouts on areas unrelated to this diff (templates list, template editor, subject picker) — reproduced clean (11/11 passed) on a second run at PW_WORKERS=2, confirming those were resource-contention noise from a cold, fully-parallel first run rather than product defects, and are excluded from this verdict. The 3 signature-providers.spec.ts failures below reproduced identically across both runs and a third isolated -g run.

findings.symbol: TC-04-E2E-01: an admin switches the organization to SignWell
findings.claim: `await signwell.check()` never completes: Playwright reports " intercepts pointer events" and retries the click for the full 30s timeout, on both the first attempt and the retry.

witness.detail: apps DS `Radio` (1_DS for dev/components/forms/Radio.jsx, unmodified by this diff) renders its real `<input type="radio">` visually hidden with `pointerEvents: 'none'`, so Playwright's `.check()` — which requires the target element itself to receive the event — can never satisfy its actionability check; the pointer event is always intercepted by the decorative dot `<span>` sitting on top. I verified a real user is not blocked: a manual Playwright script clicking the visible option row (`page.getByTestId('signing-provider-option-signwell').click({position:{x:200,y:20}})`) instead of `.check()` on the hidden input toggles the radio correctly in one click. Trace of the failing run: e2e/test-results/signature-providers-Spec-0-dde9f-he-organization-to-SignWell-chromium-retry1/trace.zip

findings.suggestedFix: In the test, select the provider by clicking the visible option row/label (e.g. `page.getByTestId('signing-provider-option-signwell').click()`) rather than calling `.check()` on the DS Radio's hidden input.

findings.symbol: TC-04-E2E-02: the signing page hosts the widget on our origin
findings.claim: The spec's own expected result for this case is "`sign-embedded-loading` appears and is replaced by `sign-embedded-frame`", but the test never observes the loading placeholder: `expect(signer.getByTestId('sign-embedded-loading')).toBeVisible()` fails with "element(s) not found" on both the first attempt and the retry, in two independent full runs.

witness.detail: apps/web/app/sign/[token]/EmbeddedSigning.tsx unmounts the placeholder (rather than merely hiding it) once the iframe's own `onLoad` fires (`{(!ready || loading || !url) && placeholder()}`). Against the in-process SignWell stub the iframe's `load` resolves fast enough that the placeholder is gone before Playwright's assertion polls for it, on every run observed. Trace: e2e/test-results/signature-providers-Spec-0-6ce3f-ts-the-widget-on-our-origin-chromium-retry1/trace.zip (page snapshot at failure shows the iframe already present, loading test-id absent).

findings.suggestedFix: Either make the transition reliably observable (e.g. hold the placeholder for a minimum tick, or gate the stub's response so the frame's load is not synchronous with page.goto), or assert the loading→frame handoff without depending on the placeholder still being mounted by the time the first assertion runs (e.g. race `sign-embedded-loading` against `sign-embedded-frame` immediately after `goto`).

findings.symbol: TC-04-E2E-04: a manager sees the setting but cannot change it
findings.claim: `await page.getByTestId('logout-button').click()` times out after 30s waiting for the element, on both the first attempt and the retry.

witness.detail: The topbar only exposes `logout-button` inside the account menu opened by `topbar-account-button` — the established pattern in e2e/tests/app-shell.spec.ts:34-35 is `await page.getByTestId('topbar-account-button').click(); await page.getByTestId('logout-button').click();`. This test clicks `logout-button` directly without opening the menu first, so the element never appears. Screenshot: e2e/test-results/signature-providers-Spec-0-53f97-etting-but-cannot-change-it-chromium-retry1/test-failed-1.png shows the topbar with only the account avatar button visible, no logout control.

priorFindingsAddressed.detail: Re-read and executed apps/api/test/signwell-client.spec.ts (all 6 cases pass, including the 3 the prior finding named): 'does not repeat a create that may have landed, and adopts what it finds' asserts exactly one POST and one lookup after the single backoff before returning the adopted document; the 5xx-with-nothing-found case shows 2 requests/1 lookup; the 429 case shows 0 lookups/3 requests. This falsifies the previously reported defect — createOrAdopt's beforeUnsafeRetry callback runs the orphan lookup inside the retry loop, before any repeat POST, not after the loop gives up.
